items.followUp: Using the head-to-tail rule, explain how to find the resultant of three forces acting in different directions.

rubric.why: Shows how the force vectors are arranged.
rubric.description: Place the tail of each successive force vector at the head of the previous one.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing the head-to-tail arrangement.

rubric.why: Identifies the direction and endpoints of the resultant.
rubric.description: The resultant is drawn from the tail of the first force to the head of the last force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving the correct endpoints of the resultant.

modelAnswer: Place the tail of each successive force vector at the head of the previous one.
Draw the resultant from the tail of the first force to the head of the last force.

items.followUp: What is a contact force? Give one example.

rubric.why: States that a field force does not require physical contact.
rubric.description: A field force acts without physical contact between objects.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the force acts without contact or at a distance.

rubric.why: Connects gravity with action through a field.
rubric.description: Gravitational force acts through a gravitational field.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explicitly associating gravitational force with a field.

modelAnswer: A field force acts between objects without physical contact.
Gravitational force acts through a gravitational field, so it is a field force.

items.followUp: What is GPS, and what does it help a user determine?

rubric.why: Gives the correct expansion of GPS.
rubric.description: GPS stands for Global Positioning System.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct full form.

rubric.why: States the main function of GPS.
rubric.description: GPS uses signals from satellites to determine the position or location of a receiver.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that GPS determines position or location; mention of satellites is desirable but not required.

modelAnswer: GPS stands for Global Positioning System.
It uses signals from satellites to determine the position of a receiver on Earth.

items.followUp: Define kinetic energy and give one example of an object that has it.

rubric.why: Defines mechanical energy as the combination of kinetic and potential energy.
rubric.description: Mechanical energy is the sum of an object's kinetic energy and potential energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that mechanical energy includes kinetic and potential energy.

rubric.why: Provides a suitable example of mechanical energy.
rubric.description: A swinging pendulum is an example of an object possessing mechanical energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid example.

modelAnswer: Mechanical energy is the sum of the kinetic energy and potential energy of an object.
Example: A swinging pendulum has mechanical energy.

items.followUp: What is nuclear energy? Give one peaceful use of it.

rubric.why: Identifies the origin of nuclear energy.
rubric.description: Nuclear energy is energy released during nuclear reactions such as fission or fusion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking nuclear energy to a nuclear reaction, fission, or fusion.

rubric.description: A peaceful use of nuclear energy is generating electricity in a nuclear power plant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid peaceful use, such as electricity generation or medical treatment.

modelAnswer: Nuclear energy is the energy released during nuclear reactions such as fission or fusion.
A peaceful use of nuclear energy is the generation of electricity in a nuclear power plant.

items.followUp: A machine receives 500 J of energy and gives 350 J of useful output. Calculate its efficiency as a percentage.

rubric.why: Shows the correct ratio used to define efficiency.
rubric.description: Efficiency is the ratio of useful output energy (or work) to input energy (or work).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct output-to-input ratio.

rubric.why: Shows that the efficiency is expressed as a percentage.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for multiplying the ratio by 100 to express it as a percentage.

modelAnswer: Efficiency is the ratio of useful output energy to input energy.

items.followUp: Name two devices that use Pascal's law.

rubric.why: Recognises a valid application of Pascal's law.
rubric.description: One application is a hydraulic press, hydraulic lift, or hydraulic brake.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid application.

rubric.why: Recognises a second application of Pascal's law.
rubric.description: A second application may be a different hydraulic device, such as a press, lift, or brake.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second distinct valid application.

modelAnswer: Two applications of Pascal's law are the hydraulic press and hydraulic brakes.

rubric.why: Identifies evaporation as the change from liquid to vapour.
rubric.description: Evaporation is the change of a liquid into vapour.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that liquid changes into vapour.

rubric.description: Evaporation occurs at the surface of a liquid and can take place below its boiling point.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that evaporation occurs at the surface or below the boiling point.

modelAnswer: Evaporation is the change of a liquid into vapour from its surface.
It can take place at temperatures below the boiling point.
